topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic and cellular foundations of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arising in susceptible cells can support clonal evolution towards cancer within a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Evaluating environmental contributions to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence that environmental exposures influence cancer risk rather than cancer being attributable simply to chance or inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a detailed example of cooperating infectious influences.

topics.label: Mechanisms of environmentally induced DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens damage DNA and generate mutations, including the influence of metabolic activation on their effects.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutation-initiating activity from the promotion of tumour growth and explain why both can be necessary for cancer development.

topics.label: Context-dependent carcinogenesis and mechanistic recap
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how susceptibility depends on cellular context and developmental stage, concluding with a synthesis of the carcinogenic mechanisms discussed.

topics.label: Methods for establishing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how carcinogenic effects can be identified and assessed, emphasizing the evidential limits of available methods.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit perspective
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by recapping its conclusions and placing cancer risks within everyday risk–benefit decisions.
